record.title: The ten-triangle conjecture for acute spherical diangles
record.statement:
An **acute spherical diangle** is a spherical diangle whose relevant angles are acute. A dissection is a subdivision into spherical triangles, and the triangles are acute when all their angles are acute.

**Ten-triangle conjecture.** Any dissection of an acute spherical diangle into acute spherical triangles requires at least ten triangles.

The paper proves a lower bound of nine triangles and does not establish whether ten is attainable as the minimum; proving this conjecture would strengthen the corresponding lower bound for gentile acute tetrahedra.

record.title: Huang–Ji–Yin Gap Conjecture for CR mappings between spheres
record.statement:
For $n\geq 2$, let $\kappa_0$ be the largest integer such that

$$
(\kappa-1)n+\kappa\leq \sum_{i=0}^{\kappa-1}(n-i)-1,
$$

and define

$$
I_\kappa=\{j\in\mathbb N:(\kappa-1)n+\kappa\leq j\leq \sum_{i=0}^{\kappa-1}(n-i)-1\},\qquad \kappa=1,\ldots,\kappa_0.
$$

Let $f\colon\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb S^N$ be a sufficiently smooth CR mapping. **Huang–Ji–Yin Gap Conjecture.** If $N-n\in I_\kappa$, then there exists an integer $n\leq N_0<N$ with

$$
N_0-n\leq (\kappa-1)n-\kappa-1
$$

and an affine complex subspace $A^{N_0+1}$ of dimension $N_0+1$ such that $f(\mathbb S^n)\subset S^N\cap A^{N_0+1}$. This predicts rigidity of CR mappings in the specified codimension gaps, but the source presents it as an unresolved conjecture and uses it as the geometric statement implied by the SOS conjecture.

record.title: SOS conjecture on linear ranks of polynomial mappings
record.statement:
Let $P(z)=(P^1(z),\ldots,P^q(z))$ be a polynomial mapping in $z=(z^1,\ldots,z^n)\in\mathbb C^n$, and let $A(z,\bar z)$ be a Hermitian polynomial satisfying

$$
\lVert P(z)\rVert^2=A(z,\bar z)\lVert z\rVert^2.
$$

If $r$ denotes the linear rank of $P(z)$, and $\kappa_0$ is the largest integer satisfying the defining inequality for $\kappa_0$, **SOS Conjecture.** Either

$$
r\geq (\kappa_0+1)n-\frac{\kappa_0(\kappa_0+1)}{2}-1,
$$

or there exists an integer $1\leq\kappa\leq\kappa_0<n$ such that

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{\kappa-1}(n-i)=n\kappa-\frac{\kappa(\kappa-1)}{2}\leq r\leq \kappa n.
$$

The conjecture concerns the possible gaps in linear ranks of polynomial sums-of-squares identities and is presented as the algebraic statement from which the HJY Gap Conjecture follows.

record.title: Weak-order maximality conjecture for affine Weyl group cores
record.statement:
Let $\widetilde{W}$ be a simply-laced affine Weyl group with Coxeter number $h$, let $b$ be coprime to $h$, and let $\mathcal{S}_\Phi(b)$ be the relevant Sommers region. Let $\widetilde{w}_b$ be the distinguished affine Weyl group element associated with $b$, and regard dominant elements as elements of $\widetilde{W}/W$. **Weak-order maximality conjecture.** The element $\widetilde{w}_b$ is maximal in the weak order on $\widetilde{W}/W$ among all dominant elements

$$
\left\{\widetilde{w} \in \widetilde{W}/W: \widetilde{w}^{-1}(0) \in \mathcal{S}_\Phi(b)\right\}.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the proved uniqueness of the maximum of the size statistic by predicting containment of the relevant inversion sets. It generalizes J. Vandehey's result for ordinary $(a,b)$-cores.

record.title: The conjecture on the minimum negative difference set size
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $N$. Let $e=\exp G$ be the exponent of $G$, meaning the least common multiple of the orders of the elements of $G$. For $1\leq r\leq N$, define

$$
D(N,e,r)=\{d_1d_2\mid d_1\in D(N/e),\ d_2\in D(e),\ d_1e\geq r\}.
$$

Here $\rho_G^-(r)$ denotes the minimum size of the negative difference set associated with an $r$-element subset of $G$.

**Negative difference-set conjecture.** Under these hypotheses,

$$
\rho_G^-(r)=\min_{d\in D(N,e,r)}d\left(2\left\lceil\frac{r}{d}\right\rceil-1\right).
$$

The preceding result gives the displayed quantity as an upper bound for $\rho_G^-(r)$, while no explicit formula for $\rho_G^-(r)$ was known in the source. The conjecture asserts that this upper bound is always sharp.

record.title: Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture for decompositions of complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $[K_n,P]$ be a decomposition into induced subgraphs. Its chromatic index $chi'([K_n,P])$ is the smallest number of colors in a coloring that assigns one color to each member of $P$, with intersecting members receiving different colors. **Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.** Every decomposition $[K_n,P]$ satisfies

$$
\chi'([K_n,P])\leq n.
$$

This is the graph-decomposition formulation of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture, originally posed in terms of coloring $n$ sets of size $n$ whose pairwise intersections have size at most one. The source uses quasigroups and complete digraphs to construct new families of decompositions satisfying the conjectured bound; the general conjecture is presented without a resolution here.

record.title: The minimum-cycle conjecture for non-b$k$d-colourable graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $k$ be a positive integer. A cycle has length $0\bmod k$ when its length is divisible by $k$.

**Minimum-cycle conjecture.** If $\chi(G)>k$, then $G$ contains at least

$$
\frac{(k+1)(k-1)!}{2}
$$

cycles of length $0\bmod k$.

The complete graph $K_{k+1}$ has precisely this many cycles of length $0\bmod k$, so the conjecture asserts that it is extremal among graphs that are not $k$-colourable. It strengthens the preceding lower bound of $(k-1)!/2$ cycles and is posed as an open question.

record.title: The minimum hyperplane-covering conjecture for finite grids
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring, and let $A_1,\dots,A_n\subset R$ be nonempty (but possibly infinite) subsets. Let $\mathcal{H}=\{H_j\}_{j\in J}$ be a covering of the grid

$$
A=\prod_{i=1}^n A_i
$$

by hyperplanes. **The minimum hyperplane-covering conjecture.** Then

$$
\#J\geq\min_{i=1}^n\#A_i.
$$

This extends the finite-grid lower bound for hyperplane coverings to possibly infinite coordinate sets; the supplied text does not indicate whether the assertion is known in this generality.

\chi'_{\sum}(G) \leq \Delta(G)+2.

record.title: The Main Conjecture on AIM loops
record.statement:
Let $Q$ be an **AIM loop**, meaning that its inner mapping group $\operatorname{Inn}(Q)$ is abelian. Let $N(Q)$ denote the nucleus of $Q$ and $Z(Q)$ its center; the factor loop $Q/N(Q)$ is understood to be defined, so $N(Q)$ is normal in $Q$.

**The Main Conjecture.** The quotient $Q/N(Q)$ is an abelian group and $Q/Z(Q)$ is a group. In particular, $Q$ is nilpotent of class at most $3$.

The conjecture is motivated by the structure of known loops of Csörgő type and is stronger than the asserted nilpotency-class bound. It does not impose a finiteness assumption; the source notes that it might hold for all finite AIM loops while admitting an infinite counterexample. The earlier claim that every AIM loop has nilpotency class at most $2$ was disproved, so this structural replacement remains open.

record.title: The sharp trilinear inequality for antipodally symmetric functions on the circle
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}^1$ denote the unit circle, let $\mathrm{d}\Sigma_{\vec{\omega}}$ be the measure on $(\mathbb{S}^1)^6$ used in the preceding restriction identity, and let $f\in L^2(\mathbb{S}^1)$ be nonnegative and **antipodally symmetric**, meaning $f(-\omega)=f(\omega)$ for every $\omega\in\mathbb{S}^1$. Then

**The trilinear inequality.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\int_{(\mathbb{S}^1)^6} f(\omega_1)f(\omega_2)f(\omega_3)f(\omega_4)f(\omega_5)f(\omega_6)\bigl(|\omega_4+\omega_5+\omega_6|^2-1\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\Sigma_{\vec{\omega}}\\
&\qquad\leq \int_{(\mathbb{S}^1)^6} f(\omega_1)^2f(\omega_2)^2f(\omega_3)^2\bigl(|\omega_4+\omega_5+\omega_6|^2-1\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\Sigma_{\vec{\omega}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This inequality is posed as the step needed to continue the proof of the sharp $L^2$ Fourier restriction inequality for the circle; because the weight $|\omega_4+\omega_5+\omega_6|^2-1$ can be negative, the usual Cauchy–Schwarz argument does not apply directly. record.statement:

Write $D^b(X)$ and $D^b(Y)$ for their bounded derived categories, and let $Pic^0(X)_{dg}$ and $Pic^0(Y)_{dg}$ denote the connected components of the structure sheaves in the derived moduli stacks of perfect complexes; these are the **derived Jacobians**.

record.statement:
Consider the online power-of-choices geometric graph process on $n$ vertices, with radius

record.title: The formula for $W_{\mathbb N^*}(2^g+1)$
record.statement:
Let $W_{\mathbb N^*}(m)$ denote the $m$-th entry of the west edge of the triangle generated from the positive integers by the $Z$-process. For each integer $g\geq 0$, let $D_g$ be the largest square dividing $2^g+1$. **Formula for the powers-of-two entries.**

$$
W_{\mathbb N^*}(2^g+1)=
\begin{cases}
2^g+1,&\text{if }2^g+1\text{ is square-free},\\
(2^g+1)/D_g,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source presents this as an observed general formula in the discussion of a problem of N. J. A. Sloane, rather than explicitly labeling it a conjecture. Its status is therefore uncertain and should be checked against the original paper.

record.title: Bean–Hansen–Swart conjecture on the $(k,r)$-domination number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$. For a vertex $v$, let its $k$-neighbourhood be the set of vertices within distance $k$ of $v$, and let $\delta_k$ denote the smallest cardinality among all $k$-neighbourhoods of $G$. Assume that $\delta_k\geq k+r-1$.

**Bean–Hansen–Swart conjecture.** For positive integers $k$ and $r$,

$$
\gamma_{k,r}(G)\leq\frac{r}{r+k}n.
$$

This conjecture concerns upper bounds for the $(k,r)$-domination number, where a $(k,r)$-dominating set requires every vertex outside the set to be within distance $k$ of at least $r$ vertices in the set. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Bushaw and Kettle's piecewise Turán-number conjecture for disjoint copies of $P_3$
record.statement:
Let $P_3$ be the path on three vertices, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $ex(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. Write $k\cdot P_3$ for the disjoint union of $k$ copies of $P_3$. **Bushaw and Kettle's conjecture.**

$$
ex(n,k\cdot P_3)=\begin{cases}
\binom{3k-1}{2}+\left\lfloor\frac{n-3k+1}{2}\right\rfloor, & 3k\le n\le 5k-1;\\
\binom{k-1}{2}+(n-k+1)(k-1)+\left\lfloor\frac{n-k+1}{2}\right\rfloor, & n\ge 5k-1.
\end{cases}
$$

The formula refines the preceding sufficiently-large-$n$ conjecture by proposing the exact transition at $n=5k-1$. The supplied text does not state whether this piecewise conjecture has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Extremal Randić-index theorem for k-apex trees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-apex tree with $k\ge 2$ and order $n\ge 4k-1$. Let $\widetilde G_k^n$ denote the set of all $k$-apex trees of order $n$ whose vertices have degree two or three only and that have exactly two asymmetric edges. The Randić index $R(G)$ is defined by

$$
R(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_G(u)d_G(v)}}.
$$

**Extremal Randić-index theorem.**

$$
R(G)\le \frac{n}{2}-\frac{5-2\sqrt 6}{6},
$$

and equality holds if and only if $G\in \widetilde G_k^n$.

Thus the theorem identifies the maximum Randić index among $k$-apex trees of order at least $4k-1$ and characterizes all extremal graphs by their degree and asymmetric-edge structure.

$$
\Delta_n(k)=\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n}{k-1}.
$$

**Minimum-width conjecture.** For $n\gg m$,

$$
h_n(m,l)=\sum_{j\geq0}\Delta_n(m-jc)=\Delta_n(m)+\Delta_n(m-c)+\Delta_n(m-2c)+\cdots.
$$

record.title: The equality conjecture for level-width and cutset-width in the truncated Boolean lattice
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ and let ${\cal B}_n(m,l)$ be the truncated Boolean lattice consisting of all subsets of $[n]$ of sizes from $m$ through $l$. A **cutset** is a collection meeting every maximal saturated chain. Let $h_n(m,l)$ be the minimum width of a cutset, and let $g_n(m,l)$ be the smallest $k$ for which there is a cutset containing at most $k$ nodes at each level. **Equality conjecture.** If $0\leq m\leq l\leq n-m-1$ and $n\gg m$, then

$$
g_n(m,l)=h_n(m,l).
$$

In addition,

$$
g_n(m,n-m)=\binom{n-1}{m}-\binom{n-1}{m-1}.
$$

The inequality $h_n(m,l)\geq g_n(m,l)$ is immediate from the definitions, while the conjecture predicts equality in the stated range and gives an additional boundary formula. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

record.title: Inverse restricted-sumset conjecture above the small-set threshold
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$, and let $A$ be an $m$-subset of $G$. **Inverse restricted-sumset conjecture.** If $2\leq h\leq m-2$ and $p>hm-h^2+1$, then

$$
|h\hat{\;}A|=hm-h^2+1
$$

if and only if either $h=2$, $m=4$, and

$$
A=\{a,a+g_1,a+g_2,a+g_1+g_2\}
$$

for some $a,g_1,g_2\in G$, or $A$ is an arithmetic progression in $G$. This is the proposed inverse classification corresponding to the restricted lower-bound formula; it remains open in the generality stated.

record.title: Bajnok and Matzke's exceptional signed-sumset conjecture for elementary abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\mathbb{Z}_p^r$ be an elementary abelian group. Define $\delta=0$ if $p-1$ is divisible by $h$ and $\delta=1$ otherwise. Let $k$ be the largest integer satisfying

$$
p^k+\delta\leq hm-h+1,
$$

and let $q$ be the largest integer satisfying

$$
(hq+1)p^k+\delta\leq hm-h+1.
$$

Let $\rho_{\pm}(\mathbb{Z}_p^r,m,h)$ and $\rho(\mathbb{Z}_p^r,m,h)$ denote the minimum signed and unrestricted $h$-fold sumset sizes, respectively. **Bajnok and Matzke's elementary-abelian signed-sumset conjecture.** If $h<p$ and $m>(q+1)p^k$, with $k$ and $q$ defined above, then

$$
\rho_{\pm}(\mathbb{Z}_p^r,m,h)>\rho(\mathbb{Z}_p^r,m,h).
$$

The equality is known in several complementary cases, and the source states this strict inequality for the remaining case as conjectural.
